note: Prompts name fixture paths relative to the skill directory. The guide's canonical URL is not reachable before the guide is merged to main, so a run gives the agent a local stand-in path for it; eval 2 withholds it to test the index fallback.

evals.name: audit-noncompliant-fastmcp
evals.prompt: I wrote an MCP server for our batch quota service and I want to put it behind the analysis facility gateway (it will be registered with prefix `quota`). The code is in evals/fixtures/noncompliant-python/server.py. Can you review it and tell me what has to change? I can't start it here (no quotactl binary), so it has to be from the source.
evals.expected_output: A findings table covering the planted violations, with file:line locations and concrete changes.
assertions: Reports X1 as a MUST: the HTTP server is started without stateless_http, and a per-session client cache is keyed by session
Reports U6: list_groups takes `user` and quota_get_usage/quota_set_limit take `owner`, which should come from the verified identity
Reports U3: quota_get_usage takes an `api_token` argument
Reports N1/P1: list_groups does not carry the `quota_` prefix
Reports A1: no tool sets annotations / readOnlyHint, and quota_set_limit is a write tool
Reports O1: no outputSchema (tools return bare str, dict or list)
Reports E1 or E2: errors are returned as an error dict or text with a Traceback, not isError with a next step
Reports X5 or E3: QUOTA_HOST is resolved once at startup and pinned
Reports B1: list_groups or quota_search_jobs has no limit or pagination
Reports I1 or O3: output is parsed from CLI text or returns a raw backend row
Uses a table with Item, Level and Location columns, and every row's location is a file:line or a tool name
Cites at least 10 distinct guide item IDs
Does not edit any fixture file

evals.name: audit-compliant-fastmcp-guide-unreachable
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check before I register it: can you audit evals/fixtures/compliant-python/server.py against the AF MCP guide? Prefix is `shelf`. Note that you cannot fetch anything from the network in this environment and there is no af-mcp-platform checkout, so work from what you have. The shelf_client package is not installed, so the server cannot be started.
evals.expected_output: No MUST findings; heuristic or unchecked items listed honestly; the report says the guide could not be read.
assertions: Reports no MUST finding against the server's tools for N1, N2, S1, O1, A1, E1, X1, U3 or U6
Does not report the JSON text block that fastmcp derives from structuredContent as an O2 finding
States that the mechanical audit was not run, and why
Lists the items that could not be checked from the source (for example U2 JWKS wiring, P1-P5 services.yaml, E3, B2, T1)
States that the full guide was not read, or that the audit used the skill's index of rules
Does not invent MUST findings: every finding row cites a real line of server.py

evals.name: audit-go-mcp-go-server
evals.prompt: Our Go service rigctl-mcp (mark3labs/mcp-go) is going behind the AF MCP gateway with prefix `rig`. Source is evals/fixtures/go-server/main.go. What does it need before we can onboard it?
evals.expected_output: A findings table for a Go server, locations in main.go.
assertions: Identifies the server as Go using mcp-go
Reports X1 as a MUST: NewStreamableHTTPServer is created without the stateless option
Reports U3: reserveRig takes a `password` argument
Reports U6: list_rigs takes an `owner` argument
Reports N1/P1: tool names lack the `rig_` prefix
Reports A1: no tool sets annotations (WithReadOnlyHintAnnotation and the others)
Reports E1: failures are returned as ordinary text results without IsError
Reports O1: no output schema or structured content
Reports N2 or S1: a description is a bare two-word phrase, or arguments carry no description
Locations point into main.go with line numbers
Gives Go-specific suggested changes (mcp-go option names), not Python ones

evals.name: onboard-new-backend
evals.prompt: I'm onboarding a new backend, panda-mini-mcp, to the AF MCP gateway. The server is evals/fixtures/new-backend/server.py. What exactly do I have to change in the server, and what should the services.yaml entry look like? It talks to the workflow queue with one shared service account token.
evals.expected_output: Required server changes plus a drafted services.yaml entry.
assertions: Says the server must serve streamable HTTP and statelessly (it runs the default stdio transport), citing X1

Flags the shared service token as a credential-boundary problem (U1/U2/U4): callers must be authenticated by the broker identity token, and the backend should redeem or exchange rather than use one shared secret
Flags cancel_task's `username` argument (U6) as something to derive from the verified identity
Flags that cancel_task is a write tool and neither tool sets annotations (A1/A2)
Drafts a services.yaml entry that includes prefix, trust_tier and agent_policy
Chooses service-tier (or higher) for the trust_tier because the backend acts with a facility credential, not the caller's
Mentions apply_namespace and that tool names must carry the registered prefix (P1/N1)
Does not claim the platform requires any code change in the broker
Labels X1 (stateless HTTP) as MUST, not SHOULD
